subject: Career
title: Digital Detox and Screen Fatigue
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Digital Detox and Screen Fatigue.

hook.text: Average screen time for remote workers: 13 hours per day. Your eyes, brain, and body are paying the price.

buildup.text: Blue light disrupts melatonin. Constant screen use causes digital eye strain, headaches, and poor sleep.

discovery.text: The 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. It reduces strain by 50%.

twist.text: Notifications keep pulling you back. Turn off non-essential alerts after hours. Your phone can wait.

climax.text: Build screen-free rituals: paper books at night, walking meetings, and analog hobby time.

punchline.text: Your screen is a tool, not a companion. Disconnect to recharge.

quiz.question: What is the 20-20-20 rule for reducing screen fatigue?
options: Every 20 min, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds

details.summary: Screen fatigue accumulates when remote workers spend their entire workday on screens and then continue with screen-based leisure. Digital detox practices, such as scheduled screen-free time and analog hobbies, are essential for sustaining remote work performance long term.
details.whyItMatters: Chronic screen fatigue reduces cognitive performance, sleep quality, and overall well-being. Remote workers who never unplug deteriorate gradually in ways that are invisible until burnout hits.
takeaways: Schedule at least one hour of screen-free time after the workday
Replace screen-based leisure with physical or analog activities
Take regular screen breaks during work using the 20-20-20 rule

faq.question: What is the 20-20-20 rule for reducing screen fatigue during remote work?
faq.answer: Every twenty minutes, look at something twenty feet away for twenty seconds. This simple practice reduces eye strain significantly. Combine it with standing and stretching every hour. These micro-breaks are easy to forget, so set a recurring timer or use an app reminder.

faq.question: How do you maintain a digital detox practice when your job requires constant screen time?
faq.answer: Focus on what you can control: screen-free mornings before work, phone-free meals, analog evening activities, and paper notebooks for planning. Even small pockets of screen-free time compound into meaningful recovery. The goal is reduction, not elimination.
